title: U.S. Senate · Colorado

context.text: Incumbent John Hickenlooper defeated Julie Gonzales 52.8%-47.2% in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary. Mark Baisley advanced from the Republican primary. The seat is rated 'Safe Democratic'/'Solid Democratic' by Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball.

summary.text: John Hickenlooper is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to a second U.S. Senate term. He previously served as Governor of Colorado (2011-2019) and Mayor of Denver (2003-2011), and briefly ran for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree (1974) and a master's degree in geology (1980) from Wesleyan University.
Career experience includes working with Buckhorn Petroleum and founding the Wynkoop Brewing Company brewpub in Denver.
Served as Mayor of Denver (2003-2011) and Governor of Colorado (2011-2019) before his 2020 election to the U.S. Senate.

priorities.text: Health care: says health care is a right, not a privilege, and criticizes the 2025 federal reconciliation law's roughly $1 trillion in Medicaid and ACA cuts, which he says will strip coverage from an estimated 15 million Americans including 241,000 Coloradans.
Climate: calls climate change the defining challenge of the era and points to his role helping pass the Inflation Reduction Act as a model for expanding clean energy and the green workforce.
Immigration: says the immigration system is broken and that enforcement under the Trump administration has gone too far, and calls for restoring due process while maintaining a secure border.

positions.summary: Says every American should be guaranteed access to high-quality, affordable, universal health care and opposes the 2025 federal law's Medicaid and ACA cuts.
positions.quote: Senator Hickenlooper believes that health care is a right, not a privilege.

positions.summary: Calls for a bold, science-based transition away from fossil fuels and cites his role in passing the Inflation Reduction Act, which he calls the largest climate investment in history.

As governor, helped enact universal background checks and a ban on high-capacity magazines after the 2012 Aurora shooting; as senator, supported the bipartisan Safer Communities Act and supports banning assault weapons.

Says federal immigration enforcement under the Trump administration has "gone too far" and that enforcement without accountability undermines American values and security, while also saying he supports maintaining a secure border.
positions.quote: enforcement without accountability undermines our values and our security.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 statement he said he is a yes on the bipartisan Iran War Powers Resolution and that Congress, not the President, decides whether the U.S. goes to war.
positions.quote: The Constitution is clear: Congress decides if we go to war — not the President.

positions.summary: In 2022 he cosponsored three bills to protect abortion access, including the Freedom to Travel for Health Care Act and the Protecting Access to Medication Abortion Act.
positions.quote: U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper this week signed onto three bills that would protect reproductive rights

positions.summary: In his Colorado Politics voter guide answers, he named ending what he calls illegal tariffs among his priorities, saying they are increasing gas and grocery prices.
positions.quote: ending Trump’s war with Iran and illegal tariffs that are increasing gas and grocery prices

summary.text: Mark Baisley is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate. He is a current Colorado State Senator representing District 4 and previously served in the Colorado House of Representatives; he is not seeking re-election to his state Senate seat.

background.text: Born in Hastings, Minnesota; earned a B.S. in computer information systems/business administration from Columbia College.
Career experience includes serving as president of Slipglass, Inc. and Enspherics, a senior engineer at Raytheon, and a senior systems engineer at Martin Marietta.
Served in the Colorado House of Representatives, District 39 (2019-2023) before winning election to the Colorado State Senate, District 4, in 2022.
Served as vice chair and finance chairman of the Republican Party of Colorado.

priorities.text: Affordability and prosperity: says he will cut federal taxes, roll back regulations, and restore American energy dominance rather than rely on Washington mandates.
Public safety: says he will work with law enforcement on funding and support, and end programs he says return violent offenders to neighborhoods before rehabilitation.
Agriculture: proposes cutting red tape and costs for farmers and ranchers, releasing a 'Farm Prosperity Proposal' in July 2026.

positions.summary: Says he will work with law enforcement to give them the support and funding needed to keep communities safe.

record.text: As a Colorado state legislator, served on the Business, Labor, and Technology Committee, Senate Local Government and Housing Committee, and Technology Committee (2025-2026 session).

Voted no on SB25-130 (requiring hospitals and other emergency-care facilities to provide emergency medical services without denying or delaying care for a discriminatory or unlawful reason, codifying federal EMTALA-style anti-patient-dumping requirements), which the Senate repassed with House amendments 23-12 on May 6, 2025.
Voted no on SB24-003 (authorizing the Colorado Bureau of Investigation to investigate firearms crimes), which passed the Senate on third reading 21-10 on March 15, 2024.

candidates.name: Chris Baum

summary.text: Chris Baum is running in the general election for U.S. Senate Colorado on the Approval Voting Party ballot line.

priorities.text: Lists getting federal finances in order, ending deficit spending and reducing the national debt as a key campaign message.
priorities.quote: We need to get the Federal Government finances in order. We need to end deficit spending and start working on reducing the national debt.

priorities.text: Lists reducing government involvement in daily life, adhering to the U.S. Constitution, as a key campaign message.
priorities.quote: We need to reduce government involvement in our lives by adhering to the principles of the US Constitution.

priorities.text: Says he is running primarily to publicize approval voting.
priorities.quote: I am running primarily to publicize approval voting, which is a system that allows voters to select more than one candidate for an office

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026) found; it lists campaign priorities but no statement that squarely addresses the guide's issues. No campaign website found.

candidates.name: Robert Chew

summary.text: Robert Chew is running in the general election for U.S. Senate Colorado on the Colorado Forward Party ballot line.

priorities.text: Says he would make long-term fiscal responsibility and reducing the national debt one of his highest priorities.
priorities.quote: If elected to the United States Senate, I will make long-term fiscal responsibility one of my highest priorities.

priorities.text: Lists proposals to address projected Social Security and Medicare shortfalls and says Congress should act within the next six years.
priorities.quote: Reform must happen in the next six years!

priorities.text: Says Congress should reassert its constitutional tariff authority and that he would work to reduce tariffs.
priorities.quote: Congress needs to re-assert its tariff authority under the Constitution. I will work with any member of Congress to reduce tariffs.

positions.summary: Says tariffs raise prices and that he would work with members of Congress to reduce them.
positions.quote: Tariffs are a tax, plain and simple. They raise prices for consumers, create uncertainty for small businesses, and punish our domestic exporters.

positions.summary: Lists tax reform that brings in more revenue from the wealthiest Americans as one of four steps on deficit spending.
positions.quote: enact fair and responsible tax reform to bring in more revenue from the wealthiest Americans.

positions.summary: Says families should be able to choose schools and be given support to afford them.
positions.quote: We should empower families to choose the schools that best meet their children's needs and provide support so they can afford it.

positions.summary: Supports removing violent criminals and cartel traffickers; says limited resources should not go to pursuing peaceful immigrants who contribute to the economy.
positions.quote: Deporting a drug kingpin makes us safer; deporting a local farm hand makes us poorer.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from the Issues page of his campaign website (bobchew2026.com). No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or debate transcript was reviewed; Colorado Public Radio pages could not be loaded. No stated position found on abortion, guns, rent regulation or the minimum wage.

statements.quote: We need a practical, honest conversation about how to deliver better care at lower cost while preserving the innovation and quality that Americans depend on.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Issues page

statements.quote: I support an all-of-above energy strategy that includes a heavy reliance on nuclear power.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Issues page

statements.quote: He did not seek congressional authority and did not build both domestic and international support before taking actions with global consequences.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Issues page, about President Trump's Iran war

candidates.name: Blake Huber

summary.text: Blake Huber is the Libertarian Party candidate running in the general election for U.S. Senate Colorado.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign website, questionnaire or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey found; the Libertarian Party of Colorado and Colorado Public Radio pages could not be loaded. His 2018 Ballotpedia survey (for another office) is not used.

candidates.name: Adam Withrow

summary.text: Adam Withrow is running in the general election for U.S. Senate Colorado on the Unity Party ballot line. He completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, describing himself as a father of four who believes current officeholders are not serving the public well.

background.text: Describes himself as a working father of four, age 43 at the time of his survey response.

priorities.text: Supports a federal living wage tied to the Consumer Price Index, phased in starting with the most profitable organizations.
Says the U.S. should not fund actions that harm civilians abroad and should focus on becoming 'a better nation' before acting to influence other countries.
Proposes that Senate votes be put to Coloradans directly before he casts them.
priorities.quote: I'd like to establish a system of direct democracy where when a vote comes up in the Senate, I'll put that vote to the people of the State of Colorado first.

positions.summary: Supports a federal living wage indexed to the Consumer Price Index, phased in starting with the highest-revenue organizations.
positions.quote: I want to move to establish a federal living wage that is tied to the consumer price index.

positions.summary: Says fossil fuels are finite and that the country should begin a transition to clean energy now.
positions.quote: The possibilities for the future are amazingly bright, and we must pave the way for a smooth transition starting today.

candidates.researchNotes: Sources: his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, a Fort Collins Coloradoan questionnaire (Oct. 1, 2026) and his campaign website (senatorwithrow.com). The Platform Discussion page is undated and refers to a House race; its quote is labeled accordingly. His abortion, immigration and tax stances were not found in loaded text.

statements.quote: It's time to re imagine our healthcare system and create one that works for everyone.  Healthcare for all would cost less than half of our defense budget.
statements.context: On his campaign website's home page

statements.quote: While I think that many people who have a gun should not, and while I think many people who have a gun do not need one, it is not my place to decide who, what types, or how many.
statements.context: On the Platform Discussion page of his campaign website (undated; the page discusses the Colorado 3rd District race)
